paper.title: On Union-Closedness of Language Generation
paper.summary: Proves that several language-generation notions are not closed under finite unions, gives abstract and concrete countable or uncountable witnesses, and develops deterministic appendix lower bounds. The registry also separates a source-only identification remark, a randomized impossibility, an only partially instantiated prefix-realizability argument, and a false uniform-generatability sentence in the proof of Theorem 4.4.

formalization_scope.summary: The custom eleven-card surface has seven fully covered claims, one partially covered Appendix A.2 claim, and three claims with no source-claim coverage. Nine canonical Lean endpoints cover the deterministic semantic results, while the randomized theorem, identification remark, concrete Appendix A.2 family, and a false proof sentence remain outside positive coverage.
specializations: The concrete Section 4 witnesses use signed integers and duplicate-free exact presentations of the union; component-generation hypotheses retain the source's ordinary exact-positive presentation interface.

Theorem 3.2's informal phrase 'without requiring any elements from the adversary' is represented by explicit autonomous clock-only component schedules; the source does not separately define that phrase.

Theorem 3.3 is formalized by the uncountable first witness underlying Theorem 3.1. The cofinite-negative class of Theorem 4.4 also fails eventually unbounded closure but is countable and is not used to discharge the uncountability clause.

The Appendix A.2 Lean theorem is an abstract deterministic prefix-realizability lower-bound scheme with an explicit limit-in-ambient hypothesis; it does not instantiate the concrete family or Remark A.3.
All maintained generators and lower bounds are classical deterministic semantic results. No runtime, finite-query, effective representation, or randomized probability model is inferred.
gaps: Remark 4.2's identification-in-the-limit union counterexample has no claim-covering Lean theorem.
Proposition A.2's almost-sure randomized impossibility has no probability-space or randomized-generator formalization.
Appendix A.2's concrete family and Remark A.3 instantiation are not formalized; only the abstract deterministic switching principle is maintained.

The final sentence of the first part of the Theorem 4.4 proof incorrectly calls the cofinite-negative class uniformly generatable. Lean proves the opposite, so the printed sentence is a refuted non-proof-target.

claims.title: Two uncountable nonuniformly generatable classes can have a nongeneratable union
claims.statement_summary: There exist two uncountable classes of infinite languages over the signed integers, each nonuniformly generatable, whose union is not generatable in the limit from duplicate-free exact presentations.

source_assessment.notes: The overview statement uses the two explicit signed-deletion classes presented later in Theorem 4.1.

formalization.notes: The source-facing existential wrapper preserves uncountability, nonuniform generation of both components, and the injective-presentation union lower bound.

lean_links.notes: The union lower bound uses the source's no-repetition presentation convention; separate bridge lemmas yield stronger all-presentation consequences but are not linked here.

relations.notes: Detailed Theorem 4.1 supplies the fixed classes used by this existential overview theorem.

claims.title: An uncountable nonuniformly generatable class can fail eventually unbounded closure
claims.statement_summary: There exists an uncountable class of infinite languages over the signed integers that is nonuniformly generatable but does not satisfy eventually unbounded closure.

source_assessment.notes: The overview explicitly identifies the first Theorem 3.1 class as the witness. Detailed Theorem 4.4 proves the same generation-versus-EUC separation for a different countable class and therefore cannot by itself instantiate this uncountability clause.

formalization.notes: Lean packages the uncountable first Theorem 3.1 witness, not the countable cofinite-negative class of detailed Theorem 4.4.

lean_links.notes: The wrapper uses the overview's named uncountable witness and the P02 finite-EUC-union implication to expose failure of EUC.

relations.notes: If both fixed Theorem 3.1 components had EUC, the P02 finite-EUC-union theorem would contradict the union lower bound; the formal witness then selects the first component explicitly.
Both separate nonuniform generation from EUC, but Theorem 4.4's concrete class is countable and is not this overview witness.

claims.title: The two signed-deletion classes are individually nonuniform but not jointly generatable
claims.statement_summary: For the explicit class obtained by deleting a finite set of negative integers and an infinite set of positive integers, and the dual class obtained by deleting an infinite negative set and a finite positive set, each component is nonuniformly generatable but their union is not generatable from duplicate-free exact presentations.

source_assessment.notes: The theorem statement is coherent. Its proof has a superficial duplicated class label in the sentence describing separate generation; the two displayed classes and the intended symmetric argument are otherwise clear.

formalization.notes: The canonical wrapper contains both component-generation conclusions and the injective-presentation lower bound for the literal classes.

lean_links.notes: The lower-bound wrapper uses the common cursor-zero alternating engine and keeps the paper's duplicate-free union-presentation convention.

relations.notes: These are the fixed concrete witnesses packaged existentially by overview Theorem 3.1.

claims.title: Identification in the limit is not closed under finite unions
claims.statement_summary: The paper recalls a finite-union counterexample for identification in the limit using the singleton collection containing the natural numbers and the collection of finite initial segments.

source_assessment.notes: The stated singleton-versus-finite-initial-segment example is a coherent identification-in-the-limit union counterexample.

formalization.notes: The current P10 development contains no canonical theorem for this identification example; generation lower bounds must not be treated as coverage.

relations.notes: Both show failure of finite-union closure, but for different learning objectives and different witnesses.

claims.title: A concrete uniform and nonuniform minimal pair has a nongeneratable union
claims.statement_summary: For the explicit signed minimal-pair classes, the first class is uncountable and uniformly generatable, the second is countable and nonuniformly generatable, and their union is not generatable from duplicate-free exact presentations.

source_assessment.notes: The displayed first negative-sweep recurrence can skip a finite initial block even though the first class requires all negative integers. Lean repairs the cursor to start at -1; the theorem statement itself is retained.

formalization.notes: The theorem-level class cardinalities, ordinary generation properties, and union lower bound are complete; the exact negative sweep is repaired inside the maintained construction.

lean_links.notes: The wrapper states ordinary uniform and nonuniform generation; the stronger autonomous-schedule result remains an unlinked construction theorem used by overview Theorem 3.2.

relations.notes: The same fixed classes and autonomous schedules are packaged by overview Theorem 3.2, with the countable class listed first there.

claims.title: The cofinite-negative class is nonuniformly generatable but fails eventually unbounded closure
claims.statement_summary: The class of all finite deletions of the negative integers is nonuniformly generatable and does not satisfy eventually unbounded closure.

source_assessment.notes: The displayed theorem is valid, but its class is countable and therefore does not instantiate overview Theorem 3.3's uncountability clause. The proof's separate false uniform-generatability sentence is isolated in its own refuted card.

formalization.notes: The canonical theorem states exactly the two valid displayed conclusions and does not import the false uniformity gloss or an uncountability assertion.

lean_links.notes: The class's countability is established separately in Lean and recorded as a qualification rather than added to the displayed theorem endpoint.

relations.notes: This is a countable concrete separation; overview Theorem 3.3 requires a different uncountable witness.
The false uniformity sentence occurs in the proof of this valid two-part theorem but is not needed for either displayed conclusion.

claims.title: No deterministic generator succeeds on all infinite subsets of the natural numbers
claims.statement_summary: For the class of all infinite subsets of the natural numbers, every deterministic generator has an infinite target and duplicate-free exact presentation on which it fails to produce fresh target elements eventually.

source_assessment.notes: The increasing diagonal target depends on the deterministic generator and defeats it at every positive round under the source's no-repetition presentation convention.

formalization.notes: The canonical proposition uses the source-facing injective-presentation predicate; the compatibility alias and stronger all-presentation consequence are excluded as duplicates.

lean_links.notes: The stream is strictly increasing and presents its range, so the linked negation matches the source convention without relying on a repetition-enabled strengthening.

audit_refs.scope: Generated existence, defining-module, and axiom audit for Proposition A.1; no human appendix audit is implied.

claims.title: Randomization does not generate all infinite subsets of the natural numbers
claims.statement_summary: For every randomized generator over the natural numbers, there exist an infinite target and an exact enumeration such that, with probability one, the generator produces unseen target elements only finitely many times.

source_assessment.notes: The source states an almost-sure lower bound and proves it with a summable-event construction and the Borel--Cantelli lemma.

formalization.notes: The current P10 development has deterministic generators only and contains no probability space, distribution-valued generator, almost-sure success event, or Borel--Cantelli argument.

relations.notes: Deterministic generators are degenerate randomized generators, while Proposition A.2 supplies the stronger almost-sure failure statement.

claims.title: Prefix-realizability supports an infinite-switch family lower bound
claims.statement_summary: Appendix A.2 describes an alternating prefix-realizability mechanism in which every finite switch remains completable while previous generator outputs are avoided and the infinite switched limit stays in the ambient collection; it then gives concrete individually generatable component classes whose union is asserted nongeneratable in Remark A.3.

source_assessment.notes: The high-level switching argument is coherent only when the infinite nested-prefix limit is guaranteed to belong to the ambient class; finite prefix realizability alone is insufficient. Lean makes that second obligation explicit. The concrete family and Remark A.3 instantiation are not assessed by a covering theorem.

formalization.notes: The abstract deterministic implication is complete with its limit-in-ambient hypothesis; the concrete Li/L-infinity definitions, their individual generation witnesses, and Remark A.3 lower-bound instantiation are absent.

components.summary: Avoiding-prefix realizability together with membership of every infinite switched limit in the ambient class defeats every deterministic generator on duplicate-free exact presentations.
The explicit classes L_i and L_infinity are individually generatable and their displayed alternating grouping instantiates the lower bound claimed in Remark A.3.

lean_links.notes: The explicit SchemeLimitInAmbient hypothesis prevents the generic finite-prefix mechanism from being mistaken for a complete concrete instantiation.

relations.notes: The source presents prefix realizability as the reusable alternating mechanism behind Theorem 3.1 and further family constructions.

audit_refs.scope: Generated existence, defining-module, and axiom audit for the abstract deterministic Appendix A.2 core; the concrete family and Remark A.3 are not covered.

claims.title: The proof incorrectly calls the cofinite-negative class uniformly generatable
claims.statement_summary: The final sentence of the first part of the Theorem 4.4 proof says that the displayed cofinite-negative class is trivially uniformly generatable because its schedule can ignore the sample.

source_refs.locator: Final sentence of the first part of the proof of Theorem 4.4

source_assessment.notes: The schedule's correctness time depends on the target's finite deletion set, so ignoring the sample does not provide one class-wide uniform threshold. The class has infinite closure dimension, and Lean proves it is not uniformly generatable.

formalization.notes: The false sentence is not a proof target. The linked theorem proves its negation and deliberately contributes no positive source-claim coverage.

lean_links.notes: This is a non-covering diagnostic link; detailed Theorem 4.4 remains valid because its displayed conclusion asks only for nonuniform generation.

relations.notes: The refuted gloss appears inside the proof of this otherwise valid two-part theorem and is not used by its maintained Lean endpoint.
